risk_surfaces.reason: Authentication mode selection is a material runtime contract.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Default to API-key authentication or accept an unsupported mode while claiming ChatGPT account authentication is the default.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could accept an unsupported authentication mode and continue through an unintended credential path. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Accept an unsupported authentication mode and continue through an unintended credential path.
negative_controls.procedure: Execute the authentication-mode tests with an unsupported mode and with explicit API-key mode missing its required key.
negative_controls.expected: Unsupported modes and incomplete API-key configuration are rejected before Codex execution begins.
negative_controls.observed: The authentication tests rejected unsupported mode input and missing API-key configuration before dispatch.

risk_surfaces.reason: Child environment filtering controls authentication identity and billing credentials.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Forward OPENAI_API_KEY or Codex access tokens into a ChatGPT-mode child process so stale credentials silently change identity or billing.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could forward API and access-token variables from the parent environment into a ChatGPT-authenticated child process. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Forward API and access-token variables from the parent environment into a ChatGPT-authenticated child process.
negative_controls.procedure: Run the ChatGPT environment sanitization tests with distinct OPENAI_API_KEY and access-token marker values in the parent environment.
negative_controls.expected: The child environment excludes every API or access-token marker while preserving only explicitly allowed account-auth inputs.
negative_controls.observed: The sanitization tests observed no API-key or access-token marker in the ChatGPT child environment.

risk_surfaces.reason: Persistent account credentials require separate role homes with stable refresh state.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Reuse one CODEX_HOME for implementer and auditor or recreate role homes on every run, allowing credential crossover or destroying refresh state.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could configure implementer and auditor with the same persistent CODEX_HOME or erase their authentication state during preparation. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Configure implementer and auditor with the same persistent CODEX_HOME or erase their authentication state during preparation.
negative_controls.procedure: Execute role-home preparation tests with equal paths and with existing auth.json refresh state under each distinct role home.
negative_controls.expected: Equal role homes are rejected while distinct homes retain the existing role-owned authentication state.
negative_controls.observed: The role-home tests rejected shared paths and preserved authentication state in distinct persistent homes.

risk_surfaces.reason: Account authentication is safe only on a trusted private serialized runner.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Run account-authenticated automation on a public repository, generic hosted runner, or concurrent worker without failing closed on missing trust prerequisites.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could permit account-authenticated work when repository privacy, dedicated role users, or serialized self-hosted execution is not established. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Permit account-authenticated work when repository privacy, dedicated role users, or serialized self-hosted execution is not established.
negative_controls.procedure: Exercise workflow preflight tests with missing private-repository and role-runtime prerequisites and inspect the serialized runner contract.
negative_controls.expected: The workflow fails closed before model execution whenever trusted private serialized runtime prerequisites are absent.
negative_controls.observed: The workflow tests rejected invalid runtime prerequisites and retained the serialized private-runner contract.

risk_surfaces.reason: Auditor signing material must be unreadable by the implementer Linux user.
Signing material must remain outside persistent role credential stores.
Runtime secret material must not enter exported forensic artifacts.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Materialize the auditor private signing key early in a mutually readable filesystem location, persist it in a credential store, or export it with runtime artifacts.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could create the auditor signing key where the implementer Linux identity can read the private-key bytes. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Create the auditor signing key where the implementer Linux identity can read the private-key bytes.
negative_controls.procedure: Materialize a temporary auditor key under the auditor identity and probe its readability from the implementer Linux identity.
negative_controls.expected: The key exists for the auditor phase but every implementer read probe is denied by operating-system permissions.
negative_controls.observed: The real OS-user probe found the auditor key present and unreadable from the implementer role.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could store the auditor private signing key inside a persistent CODEX_HOME credential directory. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Store the auditor private signing key inside a persistent CODEX_HOME credential directory.
negative_controls.procedure: Inspect key materialization paths and exercise the role-runtime test that separates temporary signing material from persistent credential homes.
negative_controls.expected: No private signing-key path is nested inside either persistent role credential store.
negative_controls.observed: The tested runtime materialized the signing key only in the temporary auditor secret directory.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could include runtime secret directories or private signing material in the uploaded forensic artifact set. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Include runtime secret directories or private signing material in the uploaded forensic artifact set.
negative_controls.procedure: Inspect and test artifact include/exclude rules while runtime secret paths are present under the run directory.
negative_controls.expected: Artifact selection excludes runtime secret directories and private signing material from every exported forensic bundle.
negative_controls.observed: The workflow regression retained the explicit runtime exclusion and no secret runtime path was selected for export.

risk_surfaces.reason: Remote gate observation must remain bound to the exact frozen material head.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Treat an initially empty workflow query as permanently green, miss a run that appears during settle, or wait forever on a pending run.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could conclude CI is settled immediately after seeing no runs or continue indefinitely when an exact-head run never becomes terminal. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Conclude CI is settled immediately after seeing no runs or continue indefinitely when an exact-head run never becomes terminal.
negative_controls.procedure: Execute exact-head CI tests for discovery grace, a late-appearing run during settle, and a permanently pending run.
negative_controls.expected: The observer waits through grace and settle, detects late runs, and terminates with a bounded timeout for perpetual pending state.
negative_controls.observed: The exact-head CI regressions exercised no-run grace, late-run detection, and bounded pending timeout behavior.

risk_surfaces.reason: Opposite-role orchestration secrets must not cross through child environments.
Role-owned filesystem credentials must deny reciprocal reads.
Persistent auth.json stores must remain owned and unreadable across roles.
Implementer and auditor must execute with distinct non-root Linux identities.
Exported artifacts must exclude runtime credentials and role secrets.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Filter named environment tokens but keep both roles under one Linux user with mutually readable auth.json files and exportable runtime secret directories.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could copy the full parent process.env to a child and remove only one known token while another orchestration secret remains reachable. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Copy the full parent process.env to a child and remove only one known token while another orchestration secret remains reachable.
negative_controls.procedure: Inject distinct unknown and role-specific secret markers into base and extra environments, then construct both role child environments.
negative_controls.expected: Neither role receives opposite-role or unknown orchestration secret markers after the final environment allowlist is applied.
negative_controls.observed: Environment regression tests found only explicitly allowed role inputs and rejected secret reinjection through extra environment values.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could rely on sibling directory names while both roles can still read the other role auth.json under the same effective filesystem identity. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Rely on sibling directory names while both roles can still read the other role auth.json under the same effective filesystem identity.
negative_controls.procedure: Create role-owned auth.json files and perform reciprocal read probes using the real implementer and auditor Linux identities.
negative_controls.expected: Both reciprocal auth.json read attempts are denied before either model role is allowed to execute.
negative_controls.observed: The real OS-user isolation probe observed both auth.json files present and unreadable by the opposite role.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could prepare persistent authentication stores with ownership or modes that permit the opposite role to read refresh credentials. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Prepare persistent authentication stores with ownership or modes that permit the opposite role to read refresh credentials.
negative_controls.procedure: Prepare both persistent CODEX_HOME stores, place auth.json under the owning role, and probe access from the opposite Linux identity.
negative_controls.expected: Each persistent auth.json remains readable only by its owning role and inaccessible to the opposite role.
negative_controls.observed: Cross-role credential-store probes denied implementer access to auditor auth.json and auditor access to implementer auth.json.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could dispatch implementer and auditor model work under the same Linux UID despite separate CODEX_HOME paths. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Dispatch implementer and auditor model work under the same Linux UID despite separate CODEX_HOME paths.
negative_controls.procedure: Configure distinct role users and exercise executor dispatch assertions that record the effective Linux identity selected for each role.
negative_controls.expected: The executor rejects equal role users and dispatches implementer and auditor work under different Linux identities.
negative_controls.observed: Role-runtime tests rejected equal user configuration and selected distinct Linux role identities for both dispatch paths.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could upload the run runtime directory containing role credentials or temporary auditor signing material as forensic evidence. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Upload the run runtime directory containing role credentials or temporary auditor signing material as forensic evidence.
negative_controls.procedure: Evaluate workflow artifact selection with runtime secret paths present and assert the runtime subtree is explicitly excluded.
negative_controls.expected: No runtime credential or signing-key path is included in the artifact export selection.
negative_controls.observed: The workflow regression retained the runtime exclusion rule while all non-secret forensic evidence remained exportable.

risk_surfaces.reason: Current operational documentation must describe the effective private and UID-isolated runtime.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Keep README or SECURITY text that says the control repository is public or implies sandbox path separation alone provides credential confidentiality.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could leave a stale public-repository or same-user path-isolation claim in current documentation after the runtime security model changes. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Leave a stale public-repository or same-user path-isolation claim in current documentation after the runtime security model changes.
negative_controls.procedure: Scan README and SECURITY for stale public-state and path-only isolation claims and compare current statements with the runtime contract.
negative_controls.expected: Current documentation states private repository verification, distinct Linux users, and explicitly rejects sandbox paths as a confidentiality boundary.
negative_controls.observed: The prior documentation scan found no stale public-state claim and documented Linux UID isolation plus runtime visibility checks.

risk_surfaces.reason: The validation bundle must continue to exercise authentication, isolation, workflow, CI and role-worker contracts.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Remove an isolation or exact-head regression from the aggregate validation bundle while still reporting a generic validation success.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could declare the bundle green after running only product happy paths while omitting Skill-level cross-surface or exact-head regressions. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Declare the bundle green after running only product happy paths while omitting Skill-level cross-surface or exact-head regressions.
negative_controls.procedure: Run the aggregate validation contract and the affected Skill regression suites, then compare reached test families with the required bundle.
negative_controls.expected: The bundle includes product validation and the relevant Skill regressions rather than treating a partial subset as complete.
negative_controls.observed: Dependency-scoped validation reran both affected Skill suites and retained prior product evidence only for byte-identical runtime paths.

risk_surfaces.reason: The independent handoff must cover complete specification history and carry reproducible adversarial evidence.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Certify only the latest remediation or populate the full attack matrix with generic prose that satisfies schema and length checks without reproducible discriminants.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could build the handoff from only the latest audit finding while omitting original contract obligations or earlier independent remediation sources. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Build the handoff from only the latest audit finding while omitting original contract obligations or earlier independent remediation sources.
negative_controls.procedure: Rebuild the specification snapshot from the original PR contract plus every independent-audit remediation source and map every extracted obligation.
negative_controls.expected: Every canonical specification candidate maps to a covered requirement and no required source has unmapped obligations.
negative_controls.observed: The rebuilt closure maps all fourteen obligations from the PR contract and A-003/A-004/A-005 remediation sources.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could populate attack-matrix fields with generic phrases such as wrong behavior passes and run negative test while satisfying minimum-length validation. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Populate attack-matrix fields with generic phrases such as wrong behavior passes and run negative test while satisfying minimum-length validation.
negative_controls.procedure: Run producer and auditor specificity regressions against a structurally valid matrix containing generic requirement, procedure, expected, and observed placeholders.
negative_controls.expected: Both readiness layers reject generic attack prose and accept a concrete control that identifies mechanism, procedure, expected boundary, and observed boundary.
negative_controls.observed: The prevention and detection suites each passed two cases: concrete metadata accepted and generic placeholder metadata rejected.

risk_surfaces.reason: Versioned runtime and Skill structure changes must be classified as material structural contract.
Changed documentation and current-state claims require contradiction coverage when applicable.

requirements.plausible_wrong_implementation: Mark structural-contract or documentation families not applicable even though the candidate changes versioned Skill validation behavior or current-state documentation claims.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could treat changed validation or worker structure as non-material and omit structural-contract controls from the saturation model. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Treat changed validation or worker structure as non-material and omit structural-contract controls from the saturation model.
negative_controls.procedure: Compare material changed paths with requirement risk families and require structural-contract coverage for versioned validator behavior.
negative_controls.expected: Structural changes remain applicable and reference at least one matching adversarial control for every declared structural surface.
negative_controls.observed: Risk saturation classifies structural-contract as applicable and maps changed validation behavior to structural controls.

negative_controls.failure_mode: An incorrect delivery could change current-state documentation while marking documentation risk non-applicable or skipping contradiction checks outside the diff. and still be falsely certified.
negative_controls.plausible_wrong_implementation: Change current-state documentation while marking documentation risk non-applicable or skipping contradiction checks outside the diff.
negative_controls.procedure: Classify documentation impact from material paths and retain repository-wide contradiction evidence whenever current-state documentation is changed.
negative_controls.expected: Documentation is either proven unchanged for the remediation delta or, when changed, receives explicit contradiction coverage.
negative_controls.observed: A-005 changed no README or SECURITY bytes; the prior current-state documentation proof remains bound to unchanged blobs.
